object_description: single volume on a plinth divided into two units by an entrance square
geometry_property: one compact volume on a plinth
single-storey to the south, two-storey staggered from the valley
does not protrude over the castle wall
exposed concrete with timber hall roof
design_condition: all uses are concentrated in one volume on the edge of the slope below the neighbouring school, kept below the castle wall and split by an entrance square so the small valley stays free and its original topography becomes perceptible again

positive: Spatial clarification of the historic courtyard and a simple entrance definition create a dignified arrival point
Concentrating all uses in one volume that extends little into the landscape keeps the small valley free
Demolishing the existing pool buildings makes the original topography perceptible again
The new building does not protrude over the castle wall
It is cleverly divided into two units on a plinth, expressing the two functions
The entrance between them is a small square opening onto the landscape
This structuring keeps a view from the neighbouring school into the landscape and leaves a direct connection possible
Appearing single-storey to the south and two-storey from the valley, the building is cleverly integrated into the diverse neighbourhood
Exposed concrete takes on the massive character of the castle complex while the timber hall roof continues the local use of wood
The spacious gallery-like foyer open to the hall is an attractive entrance for daily use and for large events
The connection down to the hall level and the organisation of the adjoining rooms are well designed
The hall interior is very harmonious for both gymnastics and events
The connection to the outside is attractively staged via the surrounding skylight band
The direct connection and simultaneous separation from the basic level is an advantage
Two different outdoor spaces are cleverly offered and directly connected by a generous external staircase
The four basic school areas are well organised in their basic layout
The double-height foyer is very attractive and allows sufficient movement in cold weather
Placing the psychomotor room between basic level and sports hall is ideal and accessible from both
The location and orientation of the building are compatible with the landscape
A wide hedge separates the parking from the entrance, giving the castle grounds an appealing address
The architecture creates a beautiful arrival and break area with a view of the landscape
Rotating the changing rooms and reducing the incision in the topography is very welcome
Accommodating the areas in one building on two storeys results in a compact project
Large window areas provide good daylight conditions
The chosen facade construction is insensitive to weathering with a long life expectancy
There is potential for flexibility of use and system separation is fulfilled
negative: There is no direct view of the landscape from the hall level
Dividing the basic level into two storeys is not ideal, as the upper storey lacks direct outdoor space
The direct view from the upper classrooms to the playgrounds in the green space is missing
The checkroom area on the ground floor is too small and does not yet work
The proposed courtyard design measures such as the change of paving are not entirely convincing
The castle garden is left as it is; a deeper examination of both spaces would have been desirable
The narrow path connecting the new building to the castle grounds is not yet convincing
The paved playground cannot be seen from the classrooms and is unsuitable for free play
The positioning of the all-weather pitch in the grass play area is unfavourable and reduces its use
The large north-facing window areas cause increased heat losses without corresponding gains
The project slightly exceeds the grey energy target
The large floor area and building volume must be optimised for economic efficiency
